text_blocks.snippet: Sarcomas, a type of cancer, can vary in appearance depending on the specific type and location. However, they typically present as:

list.snippet: Lump or mass: Usually firm, painless, and may be found deep under the skin or in muscles.
Swelling: May cause noticeable enlargement of an affected area.
Discoloration: Can appear as a reddish, purplish, or bluish hue.
Veins: Prominent blood vessels may be visible on the surface of the lump.
Ulceration: In some cases, sarcomas can break down and form open sores.

text_blocks.snippet: The appearance of sarcomas can also vary depending on the stage of the cancer. For example, early-stage sarcomas may appear as small, well-defined masses, while advanced-stage sarcomas may be larger, more irregular, and may have spread to other parts of the body.
